champion: Metastatic breast carcinoma to the skin with vascular involvement
ordered_diagnoses: Metastatic breast carcinoma to the skin with vascular involvement

facts.raw_span: A woman in her 60s presented with a 3-month history of pain, swelling, and erythema on her face
left breast carcinoma diagnosed eleven years earlier
treated with mastectomy, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy
left supraclavicular lymph nodes metastasis treated with surgical excision
pain on palpation
no fever or chills
Violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis on the forehead, eyelids, nose, and cheek, predominantly involving the left side of the face
Hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and dilated vessels in the dermis
nests of highly atypical cells
Epithelial cells in the dilated vessels were positive for CD31
atypical cells were strongly positive for GATA3
Telangiectatic, swelling erythema mainly involving the left side of the forehead, eyelids, nose, and cheek

concepts.why: The patient has a history of breast carcinoma and presents with violaceous swelling and telangiectasia on the face, which are consistent with cutaneous metastasis, and the presence of highly atypical cells positive for GATA3 supports this diagnosis
The patient presents with telangiectasia and necrosis on the face, and the histopathological examination shows dilated vessels with highly atypical cells, which are consistent with angiosarcoma
The patient presents with telangiectasia on the face, which is a characteristic feature of this condition
The patient presents with violaceous swelling and epidermal atrophy, which are consistent with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, although the diagnosis is not definitive without further testing
The patient presents with telangiectasia and violaceous swelling, which are consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma, although the diagnosis is not definitive without further testing
